cultural.vision_reason: A man's hand-woven strip cloth sewn into a sleeveless tunic, with characteristic warp-striped and weft-float patterning typical of Ewe/Ewe-Asante kente-style strip weaving; this construction and patterning is consistent with Ewe cloth traditions.

physical.title: gown; cloth
physical.summary: Man’s cloth, formed of twenty strips of imported European yarn, hand-woven and hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The cloth has been folded in halves and the stitching removed along the centre to create a hole for the head, in order to form a crude sleeveless tunic by sewing the sides together while leaving holes for the arms. The warp is of a single pattern throughout, with solid stripes of blue, white and red yarn on one side, and two stripes on the other, where an alternating red and blue weft pattern has been introduced by varying the placing of the weft, which is of blue cotton throughout. A second pair of heddles has been used to create solid bands of weft decoration which have been woven in at irregular intervals along each strip; these are composed of lines of red, blue, yellow and white cotton. The ends have machine-sewn hems. The garment has been patched in places.in red cloth.
